intro: Welcome to Alabanda, an ancient city in Aydın province, from the 3rd century BC. This Carian city was enriched by its marble quarries, and its temple of Apollo, its bouleuterion and a two-hundred-metre agora building still stand.
history: The Carian city grew rich on the marble quarries around it and on its black granite. Under Rome it won the status of a free city. Its temple of Apollo, its bouleuterion and a market building reaching two hundred metres have all been uncovered.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the temple of Apollo, the bouleuterion, the market building and the theatre.
facts: Did you know? Strabo writes that the city was known for its luxury and was 'full of scorpions' — the second remark probably a pun. Its wealth came from its marble quarries and black granite, and under Rome it won the status of a free city.
outro: This brings our tour of Alabanda to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
